title: An execution-oriented NetOps benchmark: generate→validate→simulate→rollback pipeline evaluation (repaired preregistration)
research_question: Does an execution-oriented benchmark that integrates LLM generation, deterministic validators, simulator enactment, and automatic rollback scoring (pipeline C) reduce the actionable misconfiguration rate by at least 30% relative to a generation-only baseline (pipeline A) on a representative public/synthetic NetOps task set?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: Pipeline C (generate→validate→simulate→rollback) yields a lower actionable misconfiguration rate than pipeline A (generation-only); target = ≥30% relative reduction.

H2: A constraint-based validator (pipeline B) and a formal-verifier+simulator pipeline (pipeline C) produce statistically distinguishable reductions in actionable misconfigurations when paired within tasks.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How do reductions vary by task cluster (routing, ACL, NAT)?
EQ2: How sensitive are primary results to model choice (primary model vs sensitivity model)?
EQ3: What are validator false-positive rates and their operational tradeoffs (prevented enactments vs unnecessary blocks)?
benchmark_scope: Public network-configuration corpora and curated synthetic variants derived from: Open-source network-configuration corpus (reference: https://openalex.org/W4392875514), NetOps public examples (https://openalex.org/W4405935382), and dataset notes / provenance collections (https://openalex.org/W7125775240).
Synthetic topology/intent perturbations generated deterministically from seed-controlled augmentation scripts (released with experiment artifacts).
model_scope: Primary hosted LLM: GPT-4o via provider-hosted API (frozen prompt templates).
Sensitivity model: GPT-3.5-turbo via provider-hosted API (same prompts) for a two-model sensitivity analysis (pre-registered).
transformation_scope: Intent → canonicalized prompt templates (deterministic template filling).
LLM text → normalized device-configuration AST via deterministic parser and canonicalizer.
Configuration canonicalization (ordering, whitespace removal, canonical ACL numbering) prior to comparison and simulator enactment.
primary_estimand: The paired difference in actionable misconfiguration proportion per task between pipeline C and pipeline A (P_actionable_A - P_actionable_C), measured across N=200 tasks.
secondary_estimands: Paired difference between pipeline B and A.
Validator false-positive rate (fraction of tasks where validator blocks a configuration that simulator would not flag as actionable).
sampling_plan: Total tasks = 200. Construction: 160 confirmatory tasks sampled deterministically from public corpora and seeded synthetic variants; 40 discovery (exploratory) tasks synthesized to increase diversity and probe edge cases. Task clusters: routing (≈80 tasks), ACL (≈80 tasks), NAT/other (≈40 tasks). Selection procedure: (1) ingest public records listed under benchmark_scope; (2) filter to vendor-neutral, non-proprietary examples; (3) deterministically augment selected tasks with topology variants using augmentation seeds [42, 123, 999]; (4) exclude tasks requiring proprietary vendor-OS commands or unavailable device models. Inclusion/exclusion rules and the exact snapshot script (with hashes) will be published with artifacts.
analysis_plan: Primary metric: actionable misconfiguration rate per pipeline (simulator-detected safety violation if enacted). Analysis: paired bootstrap (N=10,000 bootstrap replicates) on per-task binary outcome to estimate 95% CI for difference and compute two-sided p-value for H1. Report absolute and relative reductions, Cohen's d for paired binary-to-continuous transformation (where applicable), numbers-needed-to-protect. Subgroup (cluster) analyses reported descriptively with same paired bootstrap; adjust multiple comparisons with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR (α=0.05). Report validator false-positive rates and severity distributions. All code and seeds published. Pre-registered stopping rule: run full N=200; no early stopping for outcome.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test: C vs A only (one primary contrast). Secondary contrasts (C vs B, B vs A, subgroup tests) are declared secondary/exploratory and corrected via Benjamini–Hochberg within those families. All tests and multiplicity corrections will be reported.
missingness_plan: If a model API call fails (provider error, network timeout), automatic retry up to 2 times; persistent API failure for a task-seed-method combination is logged as technical failure and the task is marked for re-scheduling within the same frozen run budget if overall model-call budget allows (pre-registered). Missing model outputs due to persistent provider failure count as unavailable and will be excluded from the paired comparison for that model/pipeline only; exclusions and counts reported. No manual imputation.

risk_factors: Data leakage between training/held-out samples in public corpora causing optimistic estimates.
Duplicate or near-duplicate tasks across confirmatory and discovery sets.
Hosted-model API nondeterminism producing output variance.
Simulator/validator bugs misclassifying actions as safe/unsafe.
detection_procedures: Deterministic content hashing (SHA-256) of all prompt inputs and canonicalized configurations; duplicate detection threshold and automatic exclusion of exact duplicates from confirmatory set.

Pairwise fuzzy-similarity screening (Levenshtein/token Jaccard) with pre-registered thresholds to flag near-duplicates; flagged items are reported and optionally moved to discovery set (automatic rule).
Model-output variance logging per seed; compute intra-model output disagreement rates.
Unit and regression test suite for simulator/validator (deterministic test vectors) executed before experiment; any failing test aborts execution with logged error.
item_flagging_rules: Exact duplicate prompt/config hash -> automatic exclusion from confirmatory pool; replaced by next eligible seeded variant.
Fuzzy-similarity >0.9 -> automatic reassign to discovery set (not used in primary confirmatory analysis).
Simulator regression-test failure -> automatic halt; all affected simulator results treated as invalid until regression tests pass and are re-run automatically.
If validator blocks >50% of tasks in a cluster, report as structural mismatch and treat cluster results as exploratory (flagged).
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis excludes automatically excluded duplicates; sensitivity analyses re-run including discovery items and/or relaxed flagging thresholds. Report both primary (cleaned) and sensitivity results. All detection logs and decisions are published.
residual_uncertainty: Incomplete guarantee that public corpora represent production distributions.
Residual uncertainty about simulator realism vs production devices despite regression tests and sanity checks.
Hosted-model nondeterminism remains a source of variance; quantified but not eliminable.

budget_scenarios.description: Single-model conservative run using primary model only, deterministic pipeline behavior (no repair re-generation). Two pipelines used for confirmatory comparison (A and C); B executed for secondary analysis. Seeds: 3. No iterative repair calls. Minimal artifact-generation overhead.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Planned calls derivation: 1 model × 3 pipelines × 200 tasks × 3 seeds = 1,800 calls. Uses hosted-model API and local docker-based simulator; fits capability manifest (hosted_model_api_available, docker_available, cpu_execution_available). Wall-clock: model-call latency dominant but within 7-day limit.

budget_scenarios.description: Two-model balanced run: primary model + sensitivity model. Deterministic pipelines; no iterative repair. Seeds: 3. Includes full confirmatory and exploratory tasks. Recommended for the paper: provides primary result with a pre-registered sensitivity check.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Planned calls derivation: 2 models × 3 pipelines × 200 tasks × 3 seeds = 3,600 calls. Within capability manifest maximum_planned_model_calls=10000. Simulation workload: pipeline C simulation runs = 1 pipeline × 200 tasks × 3 seeds = 600 runs; simulation time estimated <24 hours on CPU via docker; overall wall-clock within 7 days.

budget_scenarios.description: Two-model run with bounded iterative repair enabled for pipeline C: up to one additional repair-generation call per task per seed (primary model only). Use only if extra budget available; intended to study repair effectiveness but declared exploratory.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Planned calls derivation: base balanced = 3,600 calls + iterative repairs for pipeline C: 1 extra call × 200 tasks × 3 seeds = 600 extra calls (primary model only) => 4,200 total. This remains below 10,000-call budget. Iterative repairs are pre-registered and bounded; repair calls are logged and analyzed separately (exploratory).

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired difference in actionable misconfiguration proportion (C minus A) across tasks.
power_plan.target_effect: Relative reduction of ≥30% in actionable misconfiguration rate (example: from 30% to 21% → absolute reduction 9%).
power_plan.clustering_unit: Task (paired across pipelines), with clusters for routing/ACL/NAT for subgroup analyses.
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate detectable absolute difference via paired proportion standard error: SE_diff ≈ sqrt(2 * p * (1-p) / N). With conservative baseline p=0.30 and N=200: SE_diff = sqrt(2*0.3*0.7/200) ≈ 0.0458. 95% CI ≈ 1.96*SE ≈ 0.0897 → detectable absolute difference ≈ 9% at α=0.05 (two-sided). Bootstrapped CI (10,000 replicates) will be used for final inference.
assumptions: Baseline actionable misconfiguration rate p ≈ 0.30 (conservative prior based on surveyed studies).
Paired comparisons across identical tasks reduce between-task variance.
N=200 confirmatory tasks with 3 seeds provides stable estimates; model-call stochasticity captured by seed replication.
Bootstrap with 10,000 replicates approximates sampling distribution.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=200 and baseline p=0.30, the absolute MDE ≈ 9% (i.e., 30% relative reduction corresponds to ~9 percentage points). If baseline p differs substantially, interpret MDE accordingly; sensitivity analyses will report detectable differences for alternate baseline p values.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute MDE assuming baseline p in {0.2, 0.4}.
Repeat primary analysis using only primary-model calls (scenario S1) and compare with two-model results (S2).
Bootstrap-based robustness checks over seeds and over discovery vs confirmatory splits.

transformation_families: LLM text→configuration AST parsing and canonicalization.
semantic_equivalence_checks: Execute canonicalized configuration in the simulator to verify intended packet-forwarding and neighbor/state effects; compare pre- and post-normalization simulator behavior for equivalence.
Unit tests: for a pre-registered set of 50 canonical examples, parser→canonicalizer→simulator must reproduce known traces (deterministic test vectors).
Round-trip check: canonicalized config → text rendering → parse again → AST equality check; failures flagged automatically.
automatic_rejection_rules: If parser fails or canonicalizer changes AST semantics as measured by simulator traces, automatic rejection of that sample from confirmatory analysis and reassignment to discovery set.
If canonicalized config cannot be simulated due to unsupported vendor construct, automatic exclusion (documented counts).
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Programmatic audit: random deterministic sample of 20 confirmatory-run configs per pipeline (seed-controlled) will be re-simulated and trace-compared for semantic equivalence; any discrepancy triggers automated re-run of affected tasks and is reported.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Publish canonicalizer code, deterministic seeds, and sample mappings. Mapping validation includes regression suite with fixed hashes for inputs/outputs.
residual_risks: Parser/canonicalizer may not cover all vendor-specific dialects; such tasks are excluded and reported.
Simulator semantic fidelity vs production devices is limited (see remaining_noncritical_uncertainties).

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Public corpora may not fully represent production vendor/topology diversity; this limits external generalizability (expected and documented).
Simulator fidelity: despite regression and deterministic tests, simulator cannot perfectly replicate every production device behavior, potentially under- or overestimating real-world severity.
Hosted-model nondeterminism and provider-side updates remain a source of variance; documented via seeds but cannot be fully eliminated.
Chosen primary/sensitivity models are representative but do not establish generalization to all LLM families or future model versions.
